solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pointer, little help (6,4)

blocks.note: to give a hand = to help

annotation.surface: Someone asks for a small tip, a pointer, as a bit of help.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Pointer' read as advice; it is the hand on a clock face.
annotation.definitionFit: A clock's long hand points at the minutes, so the pointer here is literal rather than a tip.

entries.clue: Name-dropped lovely type of music in cool location (3,5)

indicatorNotes.Name-dropped: N, for name, is dropped from the next word

annotation.surface: A celebrity name-dropper plays some lovely music in a trendy, cool venue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropped' looks like gossip about celebrities, but it tells you to drop N from NICE.
annotation.definitionFit: Before refrigerators, blocks of ice were stored through summer in these insulated buildings, making them a cool location.

entries.clue: Victorian transport taken by commuters (3)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the answer is held within the next word

blocks.note: the answer sits inside this word, after its first four letters

annotation.surface: A Victorian carriage or train used by nineteenth-century commuters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the 1800s; it means the Australian state of Victoria, where a ute (utility vehicle, a pickup truck) is everyday transport.
annotation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a utility pickup truck, the everyday vehicle of rural Victoria.

entries.clue: Flying by one jet (5)

indicatorNotes.Flying: letters sent flying are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: Travelling by a single jet plane.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'jet' an aircraft; it is the colour, jet black.
annotation.definitionFit: Both name a deep glossy black: jet from the gemstone, the other from the dark tropical wood.

entries.clue: As sarnie prepared with minimum of cheese (7)

indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters are made up into something new
indicatorNotes.minimum of: the least of the word, its first letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder; a sarnie is British slang for a sandwich

annotation.surface: A sandwich made with only a scrap of cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a filler word at the start; it is a chemical symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: Chemical symbols stand for elements, and As is the one assigned to this famous poison.

entries.clue: Brother in fleece with tiny tinny? (9)

blocks.note: to fleece or do someone = to swindle them
a tinny is a can of beer

annotation.surface: A monk in a woolly fleece holding a little can of beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like clothing and 'tinny' like a sound; they mean cheat and a beer can.
annotation.definitionFit: Friars of the Order of Preachers, founded by St Dominic, are addressed as Brother.

entries.clue: The biter bit! (4)

blocks.note: a small bloodsucking parasite that bites
a moment, a short bit of time

annotation.surface: The proverb about the biter bit: the trickster tricked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The biter bit' is a stock phrase for someone caught by their own trick; split it and each half is a definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the parasite that bites, and a moment, as in 'back in a...'.

entries.clue: US city leader in trouble with God when put on spot (11)

indicatorNotes.leader in: the first letter of the next word
indicatorNotes.put on: the last piece is added to what comes before

annotation.surface: A city's leader in difficulties turns to God when put on the spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' reads as a mayor; it just picks the first letter of 'trouble'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the state capital of Florida.

entries.clue: Shade of red — like an American singer? (6)

blocks.note: a bright red named after a fruit
a made-up adjective: CHER, the US singer, plus -RY

annotation.surface: Asking whether a bright red is the colour a certain US pop star would wear.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word, built the way you might coin 'Cher-ish'.
annotation.definitionFit: The fruit names a bright red, while the second reading coins a jokey adjective from Cher, the US pop singer.

entries.clue: Material passed down includes our tailored kind (8)

indicatorNotes.includes: the first word holds the next
indicatorNotes.tailored: cut and altered into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram of OUR, placed inside GENE…S

annotation.surface: Hand-me-down fabric, including our own custom-made kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' and 'tailored' set up a dressmaking scene; the material is genetic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone who gives freely.

entries.clue: Police arresting every person in club (6)

indicatorNotes.arresting: to arrest is to take hold of, so the police go round the next part

annotation.surface: Police raid a nightclub and arrest everyone inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a nightclub; it is a heavy stick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a wooden hammer used as a club in croquet or polo.

entries.clue: Delivery of an online giant? (6)

blocks.note: the surface wants a parcel; the setter means a ball bowled in cricket
the question mark licenses a jokey adjective formed from the search company's name

annotation.surface: A parcel sent by a big internet company.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a googly is a ball from a leg-spinner that turns the opposite way to the one expected; its sound suggests Google, the online giant.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket ball from a leg-spinner that turns the unexpected way, so a type of delivery.

entries.clue: Funny old American beef and ox spoil cuts (7,4)

indicatorNotes.cuts: the word before cuts into the one it follows

blocks.note: a beef = a grouch, a complaint

annotation.surface: A butcher's list: beef, and ox, with the cuts spoiling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beef' and 'cuts' set up a butcher's shop, but no meat is involved: a beef is a complaint, and 'cuts' works as a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the wisecracking American film comedian of the Marx Brothers, long dead.

entries.clue: Knight observed in gesture, delicate — anything but cheesy? (3-5)

indicatorNotes.observed in: the knight is seen inside the gesture

blocks.note: N = knight in chess notation; goes inside NO…D

annotation.surface: A knight is seen making a dainty gesture that is anything but corny.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' means corny in the surface; the definition takes it literally, as containing cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Taking 'cheesy' literally: food with no milk products contains no cheese at all.

entries.clue: Shivering soul hid: warmer at night? Yeah, right! (1,6,5)

indicatorNotes.Shivering: shaking letters into a new order

blocks.note: a mug of hot chocolate warms you before bed

annotation.surface: A cold person hides under the covers wondering if something would warm them at night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I should coco' is dated British slang voicing disbelief, like 'Yeah, right!'; the clue uses the drink spelling as a pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: dated British slang voicing flat disbelief, the same sarcasm as 'Yeah, right!'.

entries.clue: Beaten, that position in first place (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the first part is placed inside the second

blocks.note: to be in the lead = to be in first place
there = in that place; goes inside LEA…D

annotation.surface: Someone beaten, yet that was their position in first place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In first place' reads as 'originally'; here it is being in the lead.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for thrashed, originally with a leather strap.

entries.clue: Fashionable term for “hive of activity”? (4,4)

blocks.note: a trendy piece of jargon, the straight reading
read literally: the word that describes a humming hive, since bees are what hum

annotation.surface: Asking which trendy expression means a busy place.
annotation.walkthrough: The hive adds a second reading: buzz is the noise a busy hive makes, so this is the word for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A vogue word of the moment, and literally the word for the hum of a busy hive.

entries.clue: Characteristic of comic script in French that has leading man (12)

indicatorNotes.has leading: the man goes at the front of what comes before

blocks.note: an actor's lines are the script

annotation.surface: A comedy script, written in French, with a leading man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading man' looks like the star of the script; it places CHAP at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: In the manner of Charlie Chaplin, the silent-film comic.

entries.clue: Break in American journey certainly welcomed by paramour (7)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: taken in by the word that follows

annotation.surface: On a US trip, someone is gladly welcomed by their secret lover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' belongs to the definition: this is the US term for a stopover.
annotation.definitionFit: American usage for a stopover partway through a trip.

entries.clue: Monkey unfortunately killing last antelope (6)

indicatorNotes.killing last: the last letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: a little monkey = an imp, a mischievous child

annotation.surface: A monkey, sadly, kills an antelope.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' looks like the animal; it is a naughty child, as in 'you little monkey'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a graceful African antelope noted for its leaps.

entries.clue: Well, how might one spread butter? (8)

blocks.note: the manner of a knife gliding across toast

annotation.surface: Someone pauses, 'Well,' then asks the best way to spread butter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well' reads as a hesitation; it is an adverb meaning without trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: without a hitch, and the way a knife should glide butter across toast.

entries.clue: Spiffing idea in puff? (6)

blocks.note: British schoolboy slang for a clever scheme; spiffing = excellent

annotation.surface: A splendid idea arrives in a puff of smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spiffing' is old-fashioned British slang for excellent, the language of jolly schoolboy stories.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: schoolboy slang for a clever scheme, and a gasping, puffing breath.

entries.clue: Money in silver immediately flipped (5)

indicatorNotes.flipped: turned over so it reads backwards

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: Cash in silver coins, tossed straight away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipped' suggests tossing a coin but tells you to reverse AGNOW.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: British slang for cash, like dosh or readies.

entries.clue: Market and pub surrounding plaza out of place (6)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: the pub goes round the next part
indicatorNotes.out of: the letters of place are removed

blocks.note: PLAZA without PL, the abbreviation for place; goes inside B…AR

annotation.surface: A market and a pub around a square that seems out of place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of place' looks like one idiom; it means take PL, short for place (as in street names), out of PLAZA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, especially for a Middle Eastern covered market.

entries.clue: Lentil dish and two ducks on red or white hot plate (8)

blocks.note: vin is French for wine, red or white
dal is an Indian lentil dish
a duck is a zero score in cricket, O

annotation.surface: A menu at an Indian restaurant: lentils, duck, and wine with a hot plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot plate' sounds like a stove ring; it is a plateful of fiery curry.
annotation.definitionFit: A fiery Goan curry, so a hot plate of food rather than a stove ring.

entries.clue: 1760 yards south of a point (3)

indicatorNotes.south of: below, so after in a down answer

annotation.surface: A spot one mile south of a given place.
annotation.walkthrough: 1760 yards is one mile, read as I for one and M for mile. 'Point' looks like a place on a map; it is a verb, as in point a weapon.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to point a gun at something is to train it on the target.

entries.clue: Language City or United fans heard? (4)

indicatorNotes.heard: the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: Mancs are people from Manchester, home of the football clubs City and United

annotation.surface: What tongue do Manchester football supporters speak?
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at football chants; the answer is a Celtic language.
annotation.definitionFit: The Celtic tongue of the Isle of Man.

entries.clue: I add no more after ornamentation, Ancient Greek form noted? (6,4)

indicatorNotes.after ornamentation: the letters have been dressed up and rearranged

annotation.surface: A writer declares they will add nothing more to a Greek piece after decorating it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Noted' carries the pun: the form is made of musical notes, not written down.
annotation.definitionFit: One of the ancient Greek musical scales, named after the Dorians, so a form made of notes.
